fixes.explanation: Prophet, huh? Nice try, baker, but that word never shows up in this verse. Chronicles says Judah prevailed over his brothers and "…a ruler came from him…" (1 Chronicles 5:2). So the blank is ruler. The birthright stays with Joseph the whole time.

Livestock it is, friend! Chronicles says "…their livestock had increased in the land of Gilead." and that's why the Reubenites spread so far east (1 Chronicles 5:9). It's like when your garage fills up and your stuff starts creeping into the driveway. More animals meant they needed more room.

Chronicles doesn't mention offerings here. It says they cried out to God in battle, and then gives one reason: "Because they put their trust in God, He answered their prayers." (1 Chronicles 5:20). So the answer is trust, not offerings. The reason is right there in the verse, baker.

That's right, friend. "…many others fell slain, because the battle belonged to God." (1 Chronicles 5:22). The text puts the battle in God's hands, not theirs. That fits with verse 20, where they cried out to Him, put their trust in Him, and He answered their prayers.

Saul, king of Israel (1 Samuel 11:15), does show up in this chapter. Verse 10 says the Reubenites waged war against the Hagrites in his days. But this verse doesn't hand the battle to him. It says "…the battle belonged to God." (1 Chronicles 5:22). So the blank is God.
